scholarships.title: Trinity College Dublin Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarships

existing.description: Trinity College Dublin awards Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarships to exceptional international students who have received an offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme. Awards are one-time reductions to tuition fees worth between €2,000 and €5,000 depending on the applicant's region, applied to the tuition fee bill. Applicants must hold non-EU fee status, and applications are assessed on a rolling basis against the deadline for their region. Business, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics programmes are excluded from this particular award.
eligibility: Non-EU fee status, with tuition fees billed at the non-EU rate
Must have a course offer to commence a full-time postgraduate degree programme at Trinity College Dublin for academic year 2026/2027
Students from China are not eligible (Claddagh Postgraduate Scholarship applies instead)
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must have a non-EU fee status with tuition billed at the non-EU rate, and must hold a course offer to commence a full-time postgraduate taught programme at Trinity College Dublin for academic year 2026/2027. Business, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are exempt. Students from China are not eligible for this award.
benefits: Applied directly to the tuition fee bill of the awardee
coverage: One-time reduction to tuition fees of a full-time postgraduate taught programme, for the first year of study only
Award value varies by region between €2,000 and €5,000
requirements: Non-EU fee status and non-EU tuition billing rate
Course offer to commence a full-time postgraduate taught programme for 2026/2027
Complete the online scholarship form before the deadline for your region
documents: Basic personal information entered on the online scholarship form
Statement discussing how you will contribute to the Trinity College Dublin community
application_method: Online application via the scholarship form linked from the Trinity Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarships page
If the online form is inaccessible in your region, contact the Trinity Regional Manager / Advisor for an alternative paper form
existing.selection_notes: Assessed on a rolling basis. Selection is based on academic achievement and the applicant's potential to contribute to the Trinity community; allocations also consider regional and programme diversity.
existing.best_fit: Exceptional international postgraduate taught applicants to Trinity College Dublin
existing.duration: First year of a full-time postgraduate taught programme only
existing.application_period: Annual round tied to the 2026/2027 academic year; the 2026 regional deadlines ran from 1 April to 15 July 2026 and have all passed.
existing.deadline_display: The official page states: "Early application is advised. Final deadlines for each region are listed below" - Africa: 1 May 2026; Central, North and South America: 1 April 2026; South East Asia and Oceania: 15 July 2026; All other regions: 15 June 2026. All four regional dates for the 2026/2027 cycle had passed before this verification date, and no 2027/2028 dates are published.

scholarships.title: Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme

existing.description: The Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme awards individual, prestigious research scholarships to excellent postgraduate researchers in Ireland. Research Ireland runs the programme, funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science. The award is worth up to €34,000 per annum for 1-4 years, made up of a €25,000 stipend, a fee contribution of up to €5,750 and €3,250 of eligible direct costs. Applications are assessed by international independent expert peer review.
eligibility: New entrant to a Master's or PhD programme, or a registered student in the first year of the degree for which funding is sought
All disciplines funded, from archaeology to zoology
Bottom-up, non-directed research, except research funded by Research Ireland's strategic funding partners
Primary academic supervisor may supervise no more than one applicant to this programme
existing.eligibility_summary: From the 2026 call the programme is open to new entrants to a Master's or PhD programme, or to registered students in the first year of the degree they seek funding for. An academic supervisor may act as primary supervisor for no more than one applicant.
benefits: Fee contribution up to €5,750 per annum
coverage: Contribution to fees, including non-EU fees, up to €5,750 per annum
Eligible direct costs of €3,250 per annum
Total value capped at €34,000 per annum
requirements: Application submitted by the stated applicant deadline
Primary supervisor endorsement by the research office deadline
Submission through the Research Ireland online system
documents: Completed online application form for the 2026 call
Supervisor endorsement through the research office
Application documents listed in the call document
application_method: Online application via the Research Ireland online system
Primary supervisor and research office endorsements required
existing.selection_notes: Selection uses international, independent expert peer review. The programme is highly competitive, with an average success rate of 18% over the past five years. Pioneering, interdisciplinary and innovative proposals are welcomed.
existing.best_fit: New Master's or PhD entrants in any discipline seeking a named personal research award to study in Ireland.
existing.notes: Funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science, and managed by Research Ireland. Average success rate 18% over five years.
existing.application_period: Annual call; the 2026 call ran 11 September 2025 to 23 October 2025, with award start date 1 September 2026.
existing.deadline_display: The 2026 call applicant deadline was "23rd October 2025, 16:00 Irish local time"; the next annual call is expected but no date is published yet.
existing.program_type: Government-funded postgraduate research scholarship, bottom-up researcher-initiated
